original_question: Let Omega ⊂⊂ C^n be pseudoconvex with smooth boundary. For K ⊂ Omegā compact, let K̂ := {z ∈ Omegā; φ(z) ≤ supK φ, φ continuous on Omegā, φ plurisubharmonic on Omega}. Assume K̂ ∩ ∂Omega = K ∩ ∂Omega. Then Omegā has a Stein neighborhood basis.
target_in_paper: No exact match could be verified in arXiv:math/9509202 itself: that identifier resolves to The Several Complex Variables Problem List, not to a paper with numbered statements Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3. Your draft, however, clearly matches the later hull-condition conjecture for Stein neighborhood bases: if every compact K\subset\overline{\Omega} has trivial boundary plurisubharmonic hull, then \overline{\Omega} should admit a Stein neighborhood basis.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the mathematical core very well: a bounded pseudoconvex domain \Omega\subset\subset\mathbb{C}^n with smooth boundary; a boundary-sensitive plurisubharmonic hull \widehat K defined using functions continuous on \overline\Omega and plurisubharmonic on \Omega; the hypothesis \widehat K\cap \partial\Omega = K\cap \partial\Omega; and the intended conclusion that \overline\Omega has a Stein neighborhood basis.
missing_details: Source-faithfulness issue: arXiv:math/9509202 is a 1995 problem list, so the numbered target you asked me to prioritize could not be confirmed from that arXiv paper itself.
The quantifier should be explicit: the boundary-hull condition is meant to hold for every compact set K\subset\overline\Omega, not just a fixed K.
It should be stated that \Omega is bounded; your notation \Omega\subset\subset\mathbb{C}^n suggests this, but a stand-alone question should say it outright.
'Smooth boundary' should be made explicit as C^\infty (or at least C^2 if one wants only the minimum needed for pseudoconvexity/Levi-form language); otherwise the regularity level is implicit.
The hull definition should explicitly quantify over all real-valued \varphi\in C(\overline\Omega) that are plurisubharmonic on \Omega.
It should be made explicit that \widehat K\subset\overline\Omega by definition.

'\overline\Omega has a Stein neighborhood basis' should be spelled out: for every open neighborhood U of \overline\Omega there exists a Stein open set V with \overline\Omega\subset V\subset U; in \mathbb{C}^n one may equivalently ask for V pseudoconvex.
If one wants maximum paper-faithfulness, one should avoid introducing any stronger or weaker hull notion than the boundary hull used in the conjectural implication.
refined_question: Let \Omega\subset\subset\mathbb{C}^n be a bounded pseudoconvex domain with smooth boundary, and for each compact set K\subset\overline\Omega define its boundary plurisubharmonic hull by \widehat K:=\{z\in\overline\Omega:\varphi(z)\le \sup_K\varphi\text{ for every }\varphi\in C(\overline\Omega)\text{ that is plurisubharmonic on }\Omega\}. Is it true that if \widehat K\cap\partial\Omega=K\cap\partial\Omega for every compact K\subset\overline\Omega, then \overline\Omega admits a Stein neighborhood basis; equivalently, does every open neighborhood U of \overline\Omega contain a pseudoconvex (hence Stein) open set V with \overline\Omega\subset V\subset U?
justification: Because the supplied arXiv identifier resolves to a problem list rather than a paper with the numbered statements you referenced, I cannot honestly attribute Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3 to arXiv:math/9509202 itself. Mathematically, however, your draft is already a nearly complete formulation of the narrow hull-condition implication that people study in connection with Stein neighborhood bases. I therefore kept the question as close as possible to your draft, adding only the universal quantifier over compact K, the boundedness and smoothness wording, and the explicit meaning of 'Stein neighborhood basis'. I did not broaden it to related but distinct conditions such as Catlin's interior hull condition or Property (P).
